blocks.text: Creating the path at depth `d` copies `Θ(d)` elements. On a chain, summing `1 + 2 + ... + n` gives `Θ(n^2)` copy time. Because each recursive frame retains its own array while the deepest call is active, the live arrays also contain a quadratic total number of elements. A single mutable buffer with append before descent and pop on return reduces path storage to `O(n)` and total traversal work to `O(n)`, assuming snapshots are made only for required outputs. An immutable linked representation with structural sharing can also avoid full-prefix copying.
